wstep: This card describes the NCHFP recipe for pickled bread-and-butter zucchini: zucchini and onions simmered in a vinegar, sugar and spice brine, hot packed and processed in a boiling-water bath.

sekcje.naglowek: Why you must not change the recipe
akapity: Zucchini is a low-acid food with a pH above 4.6.
The FDA list gives cooked zucchini a pH of about 5.69–6.10.
Canning zucchini without pickling is no longer recommended, because research-based processing times are uncertain.
The whole product must contain a minimum, uniform level of acid so that botulism bacteria cannot grow.
Do not change the proportions of vinegar, vegetables and water and do not use vinegar of unknown acidity; use only recipes with tested proportions.
White distilled vinegar and cider vinegar of 5% acidity are recommended for pickles.
Penn State Extension advises vinegar of 5–7% acidity for home food preservation and advises against diluting vinegar with water unless a research-tested recipe says so.

JarAtlas rule (cautious, for readers outside the USA): use white distilled (spirit) vinegar or cider vinegar labelled 5% or 6% acidity; do not use 10% vinegar and do not dilute it with water to make 5% vinegar; add only the water the recipe lists.
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml.
For about 8 to 9 pint jars NCHFP lists 16 cups of sliced fresh zucchini, 4 cups of thinly sliced onions, 1/2 cup of canning or pickling salt, 4 cups of white vinegar (5%) and 2 cups of sugar.
Spices: 4 tablespoons of mustard seed, 2 tablespoons of celery seed and 2 teaspoons of ground turmeric.
Cover the zucchini and onion slices with 1 inch (about 2.5 cm) of water and the salt.
Let them stand for 2 hours and drain thoroughly.
Combine the vinegar, sugar and spices and bring to a boil.
Add the zucchini and onions and simmer for 5 minutes.
Fill the jars with the vegetables and the pickling solution, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace.
Put on the lids and process.
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process pints and quarts in a boiling-water bath for 10 minutes.
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased.
At 1001–6000 ft (above 300 m up to 1800 m) process them for 15 minutes.
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process them for 20 minutes.
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m.
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage.
NCHFP times are for US jar sizes: a pint holds about 473 ml and a quart about 946 ml.
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): this recipe has one time for pints and quarts, so it applies to jars of up to 946 ml, for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l.
This NCHFP recipe gives no time for jars larger than a quart, such as 1 l, so JarAtlas recommends smaller jars.
